questions: how do i use this tool
how do i use this map
knowledge.answer:
This platform visualizes investment opportunities across Rwanda's 30 districts. To use it:

1. Select a Strategic Sector (🏠 Housing, 💼 Jobs, 💰 Investment, 🏭 Industry, 🌾 Agriculture) from the sidebar.
2. The map will color districts based on their gap for that sector.
3. Click any district to see detailed gap analysis.
4. Use the Analytics tab for national overview.
5. Use the Strategic Docs tab to browse source documents.

Hover over any district for a quick summary.

questions: what are the options on the sidebar
knowledge.answer:
The platform covers 5 strategic sectors:

🏠 Housing — Total housing units needed vs DDS planned units
💼 Jobs — Jobs needed (population × employment rate) vs DDS job targets
💰 Investment — Investment needed vs DDS/existing investment
🏭 Industry — Industrial zones needed vs planned zones
🌾 Agriculture — Crop intensity gap against an 85% target

Click any sector in the sidebar to visualize it on the map.

Housing gap is calculated as:

Total Need = Population ÷ Household Size
(Household size: 4.0 for Kigali, 4.5 for secondary cities, 5.0 for rural districts)

Planned = DDS Land Allocation × 50 units per hectare

Gap = Total Need − Planned

Example: A rural district with 362,000 people needs 80,444 units. If DDS allocates 120 hectares (× 50 = 6,000 units), the gap is 74,444 units (92.5%).

This method reflects the reality that not everyone currently has housing.

Jobs gap is calculated as:

Total Need = Population × Employment Rate
(45% for Kigali, 35% for other districts)

Planned = DDS worker target OR Gap Analysis worker needs

Gap = Total Need − Planned

Data sources are prioritized: DDS documents first (High confidence), then Gap Analysis (Medium), then a score-based fallback (Low with warning).

Investment gap is calculated as:

Total Need = (Composite Score ÷ 100) × $300M

Planned = DDS investment target OR Gap Analysis required investment

Gap = Total Need − Planned

This reflects the estimated capital required to unlock the district's full economic potential.

Industry gap is calculated as:

Total Need = 1 + (Composite Score ÷ 20)

Planned = DDS industrial zone target OR Gap Analysis zone requirement

Gap = Total Need − Planned

This measures the shortfall in industrial zones and factories needed per district.

Agriculture gap is calculated as:

Current Intensity = Crop production intensity (%) from NISR data

Target = 85% (realistic utilization goal)

Gap = 85% − Current Intensity

A district at 45% intensity has a 40-point gap to reach the 85% target. This reflects unused agricultural potential.

DDS stands for District Development Strategy — the official 5-year plan each Rwandan district publishes. It contains numeric targets for housing, jobs, investment, industry, and agriculture.

DDS documents are the HIGHEST quality data source on this platform. When a district has DDS targets, the calculations use them with High confidence.

NST2 is Rwanda's National Strategy for Transformation (2024–2029). It sets national targets such as:

• 1.25M new jobs by 2029
• $4.6B in private investment

These national targets inform the platform's methodology but district-level numbers come from DDS or Gap Analysis.
Vision 2050 is Rwanda's long-term national development blueprint. Its housing target is 5.5 million homes by 2050, which drives the housing sector methodology on this platform.

questions: what is the source of data
knowledge.answer:
The platform uses three layers of data, in order of priority:

1. DDS Documents → High Confidence (official numeric targets)
2. Gap Analysis → Medium Confidence (district-level sectoral breakdown)
3. Fallback Estimates → Low Confidence (population or score-based)

When you see a district detail, the source and confidence are shown explicitly.

Confidence reflects the reliability of the data behind a calculation:

🟢 High — From an official DDS document with numeric targets
🟡 Medium — From the district Gap Analysis
🔴 Low — Fallback estimate (population or score-based)

Always check the confidence level before making decisions. Low confidence districts need more data.

questions: why do some districts show warnings
knowledge.answer:
Warnings appear when a district is using fallback estimates — meaning no DDS document or Gap Analysis data exists for that sector yet.

The platform is transparent about this so you know the data quality. To improve: add a DDS document or Gap Analysis entry for that district.

questions: why does a district show 0 percent
knowledge.answer:
A 0% gap can only appear if the planned value equals or exceeds the total need. On this updated platform:

• Housing gap = Total Need − DDS Planned Units (not Current Housing)
• Jobs gap = Total Need − DDS Job Targets

If you see 0%, verify the source. If it says 'Fallback Estimate', the district needs proper DDS data.

questions: what do the map colors represent
knowledge.answer:
When a strategic sector is active, districts are colored by gap size:

🟢 Green — Gap below 30% (good)
🟡 Yellow — Gap 30–60% (moderate)
🔴 Red — Gap above 60% (critical)
⚫ Gray — No DDS data (using fallback)

Dashed borders also indicate districts using fallback estimates.

questions: how do i select a district
how do i see district data
how do i pick a district
knowledge.answer:
Two ways to select a district:

1. Click directly on the district on the map
2. Use the 'Select District' dropdown in the sidebar

Once selected, the sidebar shows the composite score, four dimensions (Land, Labor, Capital, Entrepreneurship), and sector details if a strategic filter is active.

Click any of the 5 sector buttons in the 'Strategic Intelligence' section of the sidebar. The map, analytics, and district details all update automatically.

To return to the composite score view, click the 'Reset View' button that appears when a sector is active.

The Composite Score is the average of four dimensions:

Composite = (Land + Labor + Capital + Entrepreneurship) ÷ 4

Each dimension is scored 0–100 based on data density, infrastructure, and verified assets. Higher scores mean stronger foundations for investment.

questions: what is in the analytics tab
knowledge.answer:
The Analytics tab shows:

• National Overview for the active sector
• Top 3 districts by gap size
• Comparative neighbor performance for the selected district
• Full 30-district rankings
• Executive briefing per district
• Methodology and Confidence transparency panels

Click any district name in the analytics to jump straight to it.

questions: what is the strategic docs tab
knowledge.answer:
The Strategic Docs tab lists every source document (Vision 2050, NST2, DDS files). Click any document to see:

• Level (National or District)
• Document type
• Target list with baselines and progress
• Gap Analysis breakdown if included
• Provenance and confidence details

questions: how do i access admin panel
knowledge.answer:
Click the 'Login' button in the top-right of the sidebar. Default credentials are:

Username: admin
Password: admin123

After logging in, an 'Admin Panel' button appears. There you can submit new assets, ingest news signals, add schools to the Skills Pipeline, and update Land Center data.

questions: how do i add an asset
how do i add a new asset
knowledge.answer: Log in as admin, then open the Admin Panel. Use the 'Submit New Asset' form to add hospitals, schools, farms, markets, factories, banks, hotels, or major projects. Enter the name, type, latitude, longitude, and status. The district's composite score updates immediately.

If the map is not loading:

1. Confirm the file data/rwanda-districts.geojson exists
2. Press Ctrl+F5 to force-refresh the browser
3. Open the browser console (F12) and check for errors

If the GeoJSON is missing, place it in the data/ folder in your project root.

If many districts show 'Fallback Estimate' warnings, it means the data files are missing targets. Check that these files exist and contain district entries:

• strategic_documents.json — DDS numeric targets
• district_gap_analysis.json — sectoral breakdowns
• agriculture_data.json — crop intensity by district

Adding more DDS documents is the fastest way to improve data quality.

To move a district from Low to High confidence:

1. Add its DDS document to strategic_documents.json with numeric targets for housing, jobs, investment, industry, agriculture
2. OR add its sectoral breakdown to district_gap_analysis.json

The platform automatically picks up the highest-quality source available.

The Rwanda Opportunity Map is an investment intelligence platform that visualizes opportunities across all 30 districts of Rwanda. It combines Vision 2050, NST2, District Development Strategies (DDS), NISR data, and real-time news signals into one transparent decision-support tool.

The platform has an Auto-Ingestion Engine that scans Rwandan news sources (New Times, RBA, MINECOFIN, RDB, MINAGRI) every hour. High-impact items are classified and added to the platform's news intelligence.

Strategic data (DDS, Gap Analysis) is updated manually when new documents are published.
